introduction:
House and Land Documents typically refer to Property Registration, which is a mandatory process governed by the Registration Act, 1908. Registering your property ensures legal ownership and protects against disputes in Uttar Pradesh.

The registration process involves paying stamp duty and registration fees, and must be completed at the local Sub-Registrar's Office within 4 months of the execution of the sale deed. It serves as an undeniable record of title and rights over the property.
quickFacts:
Important Quick Facts (2026 Rules)
  • Process Type: Hybrid process (online application and payment + mandatory physical visit to the Sub-Registrar Office).
  • Official Portal: IGRSUP (Stamps and Registration Department UP).
  • Stamp Duty: Male: 7% of property value | Female: 6% (valid up to ₹10 Lakhs) | Joint (Male + Female): 6.5%.
  • Registration Fee: 1% of the market value (Property Cost).
  • Time Limit: You must register within 4 months of the sale deed execution.
  • Mandatory PAN: Form 60 is no longer accepted; a PAN card is strictly mandatory.
  • Biometrics: Fingerprint and iris scans are mandatory for buyers, sellers, and witnesses.
  • Appointment Window: Strictly 1 hour. If you miss it, the slot is cancelled and you must re-book.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Property Registration

Note: Gather all documents before starting. Missing any of these can result in the cancellation of your SRO appointment.
Identity & Address Proofs
  • Aadhaar Card: Mandatory for buyer and seller (required for biometric sync).
  • PAN Card: Original + copies (Mandatory; Form 60 no longer accepted).
  • Photographs: Passport-sized photos of the Buyer and Seller.
Property Ownership Proof
  • Drafted Sale Deed: The legal contract describing the property transfer.
  • Ownership Evidence: Previous deeds, Mutation records (Khatauni), or Power of Attorney (if applicable).
  • No Objection Certificates (NOC): Required if the property is agricultural, near an airport, or under a specific development authority.
Witness Requirements
  • Two Witnesses: Must be present at the SRO.
  • Witness Documents: ID Proofs (Aadhaar Card / Voter ID) and passport-sized photos.
Portal Receipts
  • Printed online application form / acknowledgment slip.
  • Online payment receipt or Challan.
  • Appointment Slip (specifying the 1-hour slot details).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Pre-Registration & Appointment Booking

You must complete the pre-registration, fee payment, and slot booking online before visiting the office. Walk-ins without booking are not allowed.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1 (Create an Account): Go to the official IGRSUP website (igrsup.gov.in). Click on "Property Registration" (संपत्ति पंजीकरण) and select "Apply Now" (आवेदन करें). Create a login using your mobile number. The User ID and password will be sent to you.
  2. Step 2 (Fill Property & Party Details): Enter the property's district, tehsil, and area. The system will automatically calculate the Circle Rate. Fill in names, Aadhaar numbers, and PAN cards for the Buyer, Seller, and two Witnesses. Draft the deed using the online deed writer tool, or upload your pre-prepared sale deed draft.
  3. Step 3 (Pay Fees): The portal will display the required Stamp Duty and Registration Fee. Pay this amount online via Net Banking or debit/credit card. Alternatively, generate an offline challan to pay at an authorized bank. Note: Amounts exceeding ₹20,000 must be paid digitally.
  4. Step 4 (Book SRO Appointment): Once the payment is verified, select your local Sub-Registrar Office (SRO). Choose an available date and select a specific 1-hour time slot. Be extremely careful, as this slot is strictly timed.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Mandatory Physical Verification at the SRO

Note: A completely offline manual application is no longer possible. "Offline" refers to the mandatory in-person verification process at the SRO after completing the online steps.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1 (Prepare the Physical File): Print the Application Acknowledgement, Payment Receipt, and Appointment Token from the IGRSUP portal. Compile a file attaching original IDs, the drafted Sale Deed (printed on Stamp Paper if not e-stamped), and witness IDs/photos.
  2. Step 2 (Visit SRO): Go to the selected SRO office at least 15 minutes prior to your booked 1-hour slot. If you are late, your slot is cancelled.
  3. Step 3 (Verification & Biometrics): The Sub-Registrar (SR) will verify the physical documents against online data. The buyer, seller, and both witnesses must submit thumb impressions and iris/fingerprint scans, and have their live photos captured via webcam.
  4. Step 4 (Signing & Execution): Sign the Sale Deed registry records physically in the presence of the Sub-Registrar officer.
  5. Step 5 (Deed Collection): The office scans the finalized deed. Depending on workload, you will receive the official Registered Sale Deed on the same day or within a few working days.
afterApplying:
After Registration — Post-Registration Steps

Property Mutation (Dakhil Kharij) — Mandatory Last Step

Registering the sale deed transfers the title, but does not update the official revenue records automatically. You must apply for Mutation (Dakhil Kharij) at the local Tehsildar's office or online via the UP Bhulekh Portal (upbhulekh.gov.in).

This process transfers the property ownership name in the government's land records (Khatauni) from the seller to the buyer. Without mutation, you do not legally own the land/property for tax, leasing, or resale purposes.
